bull.b: Raised guidance and expanding AI-fabric demand indicate that Arista is capturing a structurally important networking cycle, not merely benefiting from temporary sales strength. Higher adoption across cloud and AI infrastructure can broaden the installed base and support sustained growth over the next several quarters.

Very high gross and net margins demonstrate substantial operating discipline and a differentiated product offering. Maintaining this profitability while revenue scales gives Arista meaningful capacity to fund product development, support customer expansion, and absorb portions of future cost pressure.

bull.t: Strong balance sheet and cash generation
bull.b: Cash generation that nearly matches net income, combined with effectively no debt, provides unusual financial flexibility. Arista can support capacity expansion, product investment, and customer growth without relying heavily on borrowing, strengthening resilience through changing infrastructure cycles.

bear.b: Higher memory and silicon costs have already reduced gross margin year over year, creating a durable execution challenge as demand scales. If component inflation or unfavorable product mix persists, Arista may need to accept lower profitability or spend more effort defending its margin targets.

bear.t: Industry supply tightness and limited visibility
bear.b: Limited supply visibility makes production planning and customer fulfillment less predictable, even amid strong demand. Continued tightness can delay revenue recognition, increase procurement costs, and require more conservative operating decisions, creating execution risk over the next several quarters.

Large component commitments and elevated inventory tie up substantial cash before demand and product mix are fully realized. This reduces near-term flexibility and raises the risk of working-capital volatility or margin pressure if customer timing changes or component requirements shift.
